no remarkable medical or family history

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules, along with the histopathological findings of mild hyperkeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and individual cell dyskeratosis, are consistent with Grover's disease.
The patient's symptoms of scattered, erythematous, annular papules and asymptomatic brown flat papules, along with the absence of systemic involvement, are consistent with Pityriasis rubra pilaris.
The patient's symptoms of hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis, along with the presence of well-developed cornoid lamellae, are consistent with Keratosis pilaris.
The patient's symptoms of hyperkeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and individual cell dyskeratosis, along with the presence of well-developed cornoid lamellae, are consistent with Darier's disease.

The patient's symptoms of scattered, erythematous, annular papules and asymptomatic brown flat papules, along with the presence of a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils, are consistent with Lichen planus.
The patient's symptoms of rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules, along with the presence of a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils, are consistent with Psoriasis.
The patient's symptoms of asymptomatic brown flat papules are consistent with Seborrheic keratosis.
The patient's symptoms of rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules are consistent with Eczema.
